The right-hand example, where the assumptionofapoint-likesourceisalsoemployedishighlyeffectiveatlocalizingthesource,buteven the ML-EM reconstruction in the left-hand example conveys to a user the general area of higher- LBNL Report #2001653 activity, which could be subject to additional surveying and result in a fairly well-localized source distribution. The use of SDF-capable technology without leveraging a detector’s imaging fidelity is referred to as ‘proximity imaging’, and has proven to be highly impactful in many applications. The main reason for the efficacy of proximity imaging as it relates to SDF is that the 1/l2 terms id in Eq. 1 induces strong sensitivity variations over short distances (small l ), which can dwarf the id effects of variations in ϵ(Ω ). id The benefit of the proximity imaging approach is particularly distinct when in a relatively low- countregimeandtheuseoftechniquesthatwouldincreasetheangularresolutionofthesystemcome at the expense of efficiency. Compton imaging is one such example, where for most detectors, only a fraction of events are suitable for Compton reconstruction. Conversely, if there are constraints in a measurement that prohibit significant modulation of l , imaging techniques can be important. id This is particularly true for volumetric imaging (Sec.2.3.4), but also applies to a variety of other missions such as those involving low-profile activities. A compromise between the proximity imaging approach and Compton imaging is to use a coded mask to increase dϵ/dΩ for each detector voxel. If the mask is comprised of passive material, id employing the mask intrinsically costs efficiency; however, encoding done with active materials results in significantly less efficiency loss, albeit potentially while sacrificing some imaging fidelity and inherent adding complexity both to the hardware, but also to the analysis. In principle, a detector system could be operated in a mode where the SDF evaluation of singles - with directionality encoded by a mask pattern - is coupled with Compton imaging for the coincident events.
